p0.original: Every man is rich or poor according to the degree in which he can afford to enjoy the necessaries, conveniencies, and amusements of human life. But after the division of labour has once thoroughly taken place, it is but a very small part of these with which a man's own labour can supply him. The far greater part of them he must derive from the labour of other people, and he must be rich or poor according to the quantity of that labour which he can command, or which he can afford to purchase. The value of any commodity, therefore, to the person who possesses it, and who means not to use or consume it himself, but to exchange it for other commodities, is equal to the quantity of labour which it enables him to purchase or command. Labour therefore, is the real measure of the exchangeable value of all commodities.
p0.zh: 每个人的贫富都取决于他能承受得起的享受人类生活的必要、便利和娱乐的程度。 但是,在劳动分工一度彻底完成之后,一个人自己的劳动只能用其中很小的一部分来供给他. 其中的更大部分必须来自其他人的劳动,他必须根据他能够指挥的或他能够买得起的劳动数量,成为富人或穷人。 因此,任何商品对拥有者的价值,以及意味着不使用或消费商品,而是将其换成其他商品的人的价值,等于它使他能够购买或指挥的劳力数量。 因此,劳动力是衡量所有商品可交换价值的真正尺度。

p1.original: The real price of every thing, what every thing really costs to the man who wants to acquire it, is the toil and trouble of acquiring it. What every thing is really worth to the man who has acquired it and who wants to dispose of it, or exchange it for something else, is the toil and trouble which it can save to himself, and which it can impose upon other people. What is bought with money, or with goods, is purchased by labour, as much as what we acquire by the toil of our own body. That money, or those goods, indeed, save us this toil. They contain the value of a certain quantity of labour, which we exchange for what is supposed at the time to contain the value of an equal quantity. Labour was the first price, the original purchase money that was paid for all things. It was not by gold or by silver, but by labour, that all the wealth of the world was originally purchased; and its value, to those who possess it, and who want to exchange it for some new productions, is precisely equal to the quantity of labour which it can enable them to purchase or command.
p1.zh: 每样东西的真正代价, 每样东西真正要付出的代价, 想要获得它的人, 是获得它的劳累和困难。 对于已经获得它的人来说,每一个事物都真正值钱,谁想处置它,或者把它换成别的东西,就是它能够拯救自己,并且能够强加给其他人的劳累和麻烦. 用钱买的东西,或用货物买的东西,都是靠劳力买的,就像我们用自己身体的劳累买的东西一样. 那些钱,或者那些货物,确实, 拯救我们这个劳累。 它们包含一定数量劳动力的价值,我们用这些劳动力交换当时应该包含的同等数量值.劳动是第一个价格,最初购买的钱是用来支付所有东西的.世界上所有财富,不是靠黄金或白银,而是靠劳力,原来是购买的;而其价值,对于拥有财富的人,以及想将其换成一些新产品的,恰恰等于它能够让他们购买或指挥的劳力数量.

p2.original: Wealth, as Mr Hobbes says, is power. But the person who either acquires, or succeeds to a great fortune, does not necessarily acquire or succeed to any political power, either civil or military. His fortune may, perhaps, afford him the means of acquiring both; but the mere possession of that fortune does not necessarily convey to him either. The power which that possession immediately and directly conveys to him, is the power of purchasing a certain command over all the labour, or over all the produce of labour which is then in the market. His fortune is greater or less, precisely in proportion to the extent of this power, or to the quantity either of other men's labour, or, what is the same thing, of the produce of other men's labour, which it enables him to purchase or command. The exchangeable value of every thing must always be precisely equal to the extent of this power which it conveys to its owner.
p2.zh: 财富,正如霍布斯先生所说,是权力。 但是,获得或继承巨额财富的人不一定获得或继承任何政治权力,无论是民事还是军事权力。 他的财产或许能使他获得这两种财产,但拥有这种财产不一定传达给他。 他拥有的这种权力立即直接传达给他,就是对所有劳动力或当时市场上的所有劳动力产品购买一定的控制权。 他的财富或多或少,与这种权力的程度或与其他男子劳动的数量,或与其他男子劳动的产品的数量成正比,这使他能够购买或指挥其他男子劳动的产品。每一事物的可交换价值必须始终与它向所有人传达的权力程度完全相等。

p3.original: But though labour be the real measure of the exchangeable value of all commodities, it is not that by which their value is commonly estimated. It is often difficult to ascertain the proportion between two different quantities of labour. The time spent in two different sorts of work will not always alone determine this proportion. The different degrees of hardship endured, and of ingenuity exercised, must likewise be taken into account. There may be more labour in an hour's hard work, than in two hours easy business; or in an hour's application to a trade which it cost ten years labour to learn, than in a month's industry, at an ordinary and obvious employment. But it is not easy to find any accurate measure either of hardship or ingenuity. In exchanging, indeed, the different productions of different sorts of labour for one another, some allowance is commonly made for both. It is adjusted, however, not by any accurate measure, but by the higgling and bargaining of the market, according to that sort of rough equality which, though not exact, is sufficient for carrying on the business of common life.
p3.zh: 但是,虽然劳动力是衡量所有商品可交换价值的真正尺度,但并非通常用来估计其价值的尺度。通常很难确定两种不同数量劳动力的比例。从事两种不同工作所花费的时间并不总是单靠时间决定这个比例。 同样,必须考虑到所经历的不同程度的困难和所表现出的智慧。在一个小时的艰苦工作里,劳动力可能比两个小时的简单工作多;或者在一个小时的时间内,在普通和明显的就业中,劳动力需要学习10年,而不是在一个月的工业中。 但是,要找到任何准确的衡量困难或聪明的尺度并不容易。 在相互交换不同种类劳动力的不同生产时,通常对两者都给予一定的补贴。 然而,它不是通过任何准确的衡量标准,而是通过市场之间的徘徊和讨价还价来加以调整的,这种粗糙的平等虽然不确切,但足以维持共同生活。

p4.original: Every commodity, besides, is more frequently exchanged for, and thereby compared with, other commodities, than with labour. It is more natural, therefore, to estimate its exchangeable value by the quantity of some other commodity, than by that of the labour which it can produce. The greater part of people, too, understand better what is meant by a quantity of a particular commodity, than by a quantity of labour. The one is a plain palpable object; the other an abstract notion, which though it can be made sufficiently intelligible, is not altogether so natural and obvious.
p4.zh: 此外,每一种商品都比劳动力更经常地与其他商品进行交换,从而与其他商品进行比较。 因此,比起能够生产的劳动力,更自然的做法是按某些其他商品的数量估计其可交换价值。大部分人也更了解某种特定商品的数量意味着什么,而不是劳动力的数量。前者是一个显而易见的对象;而后者是一个抽象的概念,虽然它能够足够明了,但并不完全自然和明显。

p5.original: But when barter ceases, and money has become the common instrument of commerce, every particular commodity is more frequently exchanged for money than for any other commodity. The butcher seldom carries his beef or his mutton to the baker or the brewer, in order to exchange them for bread or for beer; but he carries them to the market, where he exchanges them for money, and afterwards exchanges that money for bread and for beer. The quantity of money which he gets for them regulates, too, the quantity of bread and beer which he can afterwards purchase. It is more natural and obvious to him, therefore, to estimate their value by the quantity of money, the commodity for which he immediately exchanges them, than by that of bread and beer, the commodities for which he can exchange them only by the intervention of another commodity; and rather to say that his butcher's meat is worth three-pence or fourpence a-pound, than that it is worth three or four pounds of bread, or three or four quarts of small beer. Hence it comes to pass, that the exchangeable value of every commodity is more frequently estimated by the quantity of money, than by the quantity either of labour or of any other commodity which can be had in exchange for it.
p5.zh: 但当易货停止交易,金钱成为商业的共同工具时,每一种特定的商品都比其他商品更经常地被换钱.屠夫很少将牛肉或羊肉带到面包师或酿酒师那里,以换取面包或啤酒;但他却将牛肉或羊肉带到市场,在那里他用钱换钱,然后用钱换面包和啤酒。 他为这些钱得到的资金数量也决定了他以后可以购买的面包和啤酒的数量。 因此,对他来说,更自然和明显的是,用钱的数量来估计它们的价值,他立即用来交换的商品,而不是面包和啤酒,他只能通过另一种商品的干预才能用来交换它们的商品;而可以说他的屠夫肉值三便士或四便士一磅,比起它值三四磅的面包,或三四夸克的小型啤酒. 因此,每种商品的可交换价值比劳动力或任何其他商品的可交换价值更经常地按货币数量估算。

p6.original: Gold and silver, however, like every other commodity, vary in their value; are sometimes cheaper and sometimes dearer, sometimes of easier and sometimes of more difficult purchase. The quantity of labour which any particular quantity of them can purchase or command, or the quantity of other goods which it will exchange for, depends always upon the fertility or barrenness of the mines which happen to be known about the time when such exchanges are made. The discovery of the abundant mines of America, reduced, in the sixteenth century, the value of gold and silver in Europe to about a third of what it had been before. As it cost less labour to bring those metals from the mine to the market, so, when they were brought thither, they could purchase or command less labour; and this revolution in their value, though perhaps the greatest, is by no means the only one of which history gives some account. But as a measure of quantity, such as the natural foot, fathom, or handful, which is continually varying in its own quantity, can never be an accurate measure of the quantity of other things; so a commodity which is itself continually varying in its own value, can never be an accurate measure of the value of other commodities. Equal quantities of labour, at all times and places, may be said to be of equal value to the labourer. In his ordinary state of health, strength, and spirits; in the ordinary degree of his skill and dexterity, he must always lay down the same portion of his ease, his liberty, and his happiness. The price which he pays must always be the same, whatever may be the quantity of goods which he receives in return for it. Of these, indeed, it may sometimes purchase a greater and sometimes a smaller quantity; but it is their value which varies, not that of the labour which purchases them. At all times and places, that is dear which it is difficult to come at, or which it costs much labour to acquire; and that cheap which is to be had easily, or with very little labour. Labour alone, therefore, never varying in its own value, is alone the ultimate and real standard by which the value of all commodities can at all times and places be estimated and compared. It is their real price; money is their nominal price only.
p6.zh: 然而,金银与所有其他商品一样,其价值也各不相同;有时更便宜,有时更贵,有时更容易购买,有时更难购买。 它们可以购买或指挥的劳力数量,或它可以交换的其他货物数量,始终取决于矿场的肥力或贫瘠程度,而这种矿场恰巧是在进行这种交换时知道的。 美国丰富的矿山的发现,在16世纪将欧洲的金银价值降到了之前的约三分之一. 由于将矿山中的金属运入市场花费较少的劳力,所以,当这些金属被运走时,它们可以购买或获得较少的劳力;而这种价值的革命,尽管也许是最伟大的,绝不是历史所描述的唯一的。 但是,作为一种量度,如自然足量、足量、足量或足量,本身数量不断变化,永远不能准确衡量其他物品的数量;因此,一种本身价值不断变化的商品,本身也永远不能准确衡量其他商品的价值。在所有时间和地点,劳动力数量相等,可以说与工人具有同等价值。在他的普通的健康状况,力量,和精神中;在普通的技巧和机敏程度中,他必须永远放下他轻松,自由和幸福的同一部分. 他支付的价格必须始终相同,无论他收到多少货物作为回报。 实际上,其中有时它可能购买数量更多,有时更少;但其价值却各不相同,而不是购买这些价值的劳力。在所有时间和地点,这是难以找到的,或需要花费大量劳力才能获得的;是容易得到的,或劳动力很少的廉价。 因此,仅靠劳动力本身的价值是绝对和真实的标准,可以在任何时候和任何地点估计和比较所有商品的价值。 这是他们的真实价格;金钱只是他们的名义价格。

p7.original: But though equal quantities of labour are always of equal value to the labourer, yet to the person who employs him they appear sometimes to be of greater, and sometimes of smaller value. He purchases them sometimes with a greater, and sometimes with a smaller quantity of goods, and to him the price of labour seems to vary like that of all other things. It appears to him dear in the one case, and cheap in the other. In reality, however, it is the goods which are cheap in the one case, and dear in the other.
p7.zh: 但是,尽管同等数量的劳动力总是与工人具有同等价值,但对于雇用他的人来说,这些劳动力有时似乎价值更大,有时价值较小。 他有时用更大的,有时用更少的商品来购买它们,在他看来,劳动力的价格似乎与所有其他事物的价格一样不同. 在他看来,这在一件案子中是亲爱的,在另一件案子中是便宜的。 然而,在现实中,货物在一种情况下是廉价的,在另一种情况下是珍贵的。

p8.original: In this popular sense, therefore, labour, like commodities, may be said to have a real and a nominal price. Its real price may be said to consist in the quantity of the necessaries and conveniencies of life which are given for it; its nominal price, in the quantity of money. The labourer is rich or poor, is well or ill rewarded, in proportion to the real, not to the nominal price of his labour.
p8.zh: 因此,从这种流行的意义上讲,劳动力与商品一样,可以说具有真实和名义的价格。其实际价格可以说包括给它的生活必需品和方便品的数量;其名义价格,即金钱的数量。工者富贵贫贱,有优劣之赏,按实者之比例,不按其劳役之名义价.

p9.original: The distinction between the real and the nominal price of commodities and labour is not a matter of mere speculation, but may sometimes be of considerable use in practice. The same real price is always of the same value; but on account of the variations in the value of gold and silver, the same nominal price is sometimes of very different values. When a landed estate, therefore, is sold with a reservation of a perpetual rent, if it is intended that this rent should always be of the same value, it is of importance to the family in whose favour it is reserved, that it should not consist in a particular sum of money. Its value would in this case be liable to variations of two different kinds: first, to those which arise from the different quantities of gold and silver which are contained at different times in coin of the same denomination; and, secondly, to those which arise from the different values of equal quantities of gold and silver at different times.
p9.zh: 初级商品和劳动力的实际价格和名义价格的区别不仅仅是投机问题,有时在实践中可能有很大用处。同样的真价始终是同值的;但是由于金银价值的变化,同样的名义价格有时也有着非常不同的价值. 因此,如果一个土地的地产出售时保留了永久租金,如果打算这种租金应始终具有同等价值,那么,对于保留该地产的家庭来说,重要的是,它不应是一笔特定金额。 在这种情况下,其价值将受到两种不同种类的变化的影响:第一,来自不同时期在同一面额的硬币中不同数量金银;第二,来自不同时期相同数量金银的不同价值。

p10.original: Princes and sovereign states have frequently fancied that they had a temporary interest to diminish the quantity of pure metal contained in their coins; but they seldom have fancied that they had any to augment it. The quantity of metal contained in the coins, I believe of all nations, has accordingly been almost continually diminishing, and hardly ever augmenting. Such variations, therefore, tend almost always to diminish the value of a money rent.
p10.zh: 王子和主权国家经常幻想他们暂时有兴趣减少其硬币中所含的纯金属数量;但他们很少幻想他们有任何可以增加的金属。 我认为,所有国家认为,硬币中的金属数量因此几乎在不断减少,而且几乎没有增加。 因此,这种差异几乎总是会降低货币租金的价值。

p11.original: The discovery of the mines of America diminished the value of gold and silver in Europe. This diminution, it is commonly supposed, though I apprehend without any certain proof, is still going on gradually, and is likely to continue to do so for a long time. Upon this supposition, therefore, such variations are more likely to diminish than to augment the value of a money rent, even though it should be stipulated to be paid, not in such a quantity of coined money of such a denomination (in so many pounds sterling, for example), but in so many ounces, either of pure silver, or of silver of a certain standard.
p11.zh: 美国矿山的发现降低了金银在欧洲的价值. 这种缩减,通常认为,虽然我在没有任何证据的情况下逮捕,但仍在继续,而且很可能会持续很长时间。 因此,从这种假设来看,这种变化比增加货币租金的价值更有可能减少,即使应该规定支付,但这种货币的硬币数量不是如此之多(例如,如此之多的英镑),而是如此之多的盎司,要么纯银,要么某种标准银。

p12.original: The rents which have been reserved in corn, have preserved their value much better than those which have been reserved in money, even where the denomination of the coin has not been altered. By the 18th of Elizabeth, it was enacted, that a third of the rent of all college leases should be reserved in corn, to be paid either in kind, or according to the current prices at the nearest public market. The money arising from this corn rent, though originally but a third of the whole, is, in the present times, according to Dr. Blackstone, commonly near double of what arises from the other two-thirds. The old money rents of colleges must, according to this account, have sunk almost to a fourth part of their ancient value, or are worth little more than a fourth part of the corn which they were formerly worth. But since the reign of Philip and Mary, the denomination of the English coin has undergone little or no alteration, and the same number of pounds, shillings, and pence, have contained very nearly the same quantity of pure silver. This degradation, therefore, in the value of the money rents of colleges, has arisen altogether from the degradation in the price of silver.
p12.zh: 以玉米预留的租金比以货币预留的租金要好得多,即使硬币面额没有改变。到了伊丽莎白的18日,它颁布,所有学院租约的租金的三分之一应保留在玉米上,或者以实物支付,或者根据最近的公共市场目前的价格支付.这笔玉米租金虽然最初只占整个租金的三分之一,但据Dr.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A.A黑石,通常为另外三分之二的产物的近一倍.学院的旧钱租金,根据这个说法,必须已经沉没了近其古代价值的四分之一,或者价值略高于其以前价值的玉米的四分之一. 但自腓力和玛丽统治以来,英国硬币的面额几乎或没有发生任何改变,同样的磅,先令,便士的数量也包含着几乎相同的纯银数量. 因此,在大学的货币租金价值方面,这种下降完全产生于银价的下降。

p13.original: When the degradation in the value of silver is combined with the diminution of the quantity of it contained in the coin of the same denomination, the loss is frequently still greater. In Scotland, where the denomination of the coin has undergone much greater alterations than it ever did in England, and in France, where it has undergone still greater than it ever did in Scotland, some ancient rents, originally of considerable value, have, in this manner, been reduced almost to nothing.
p13.zh: 当银币价值的退化与同一种面额的硬币中所含的银币数量减少相结合时,损失往往更大。 在苏格兰,硬币的面额的改变比在英国大得多,在法国,其改变的幅度仍然比在苏格兰大得多,一些原本价值相当高的古代租金,以这种方式几乎降到一无所有.

p14.original: Equal quantities of labour will, at distant times, be purchased more nearly with equal quantities of corn, the subsistence of the labourer, than with equal quantities of gold and silver, or, perhaps, of any other commodity. Equal quantities of corn, therefore, will, at distant times, be more nearly of the same real value, or enable the possessor to purchase or command more nearly the same quantity of the labour of other people. They will do this, I say, more nearly than equal quantities of almost any other commodity; for even equal quantities of corn will not do it exactly. The subsistence of the labourer, or the real price of labour, as I shall endeavour to shew hereafter, is very different upon different occasions; more liberal in a society advancing to opulence, than in one that is standing still, and in one that is standing still, than in one that is going backwards. Every other commodity, however, will, at any particular time, purchase a greater or smaller quantity of labour, in proportion to the quantity of subsistence which it can purchase at that time. A rent, therefore, reserved in corn, is liable only to the variations in the quantity of labour which a certain quantity of corn can purchase. But a rent reserved in any other commodity is liable, not only to the variations in the quantity of labour which any particular quantity of corn can purchase, but to the variations in the quantity of corn which can be purchased by any particular quantity of that commodity.
p14.zh: 在遥远的时期,要购买同等数量的劳动力,就必须购买同等数量的玉米、工人的生计,而不是同等数量的黄金和白银,或许还有任何其他商品。 因此,同样数量的玉米在遥远的时期将更接近于同样的实际价值,或使拥有者能够购买或支配与其他人几乎相同数量的劳动力。 我说,他们将这样做,几乎不等于任何其他商品的数量;因为即使同样数量的玉米也不会完全做到。工人的生计,或真正的劳动价格,正如我今后要努力显示的那样,在不同场合都大不相同;在走向富裕的社会中,比站在静态和静态的社会中,比在倒退的社会中,更加自由。 然而,所有其他商品将在任何特定时间购买与其当时可购买的维持生计量相称的更多或更少的劳力。 因此,在玉米中预留的租金仅因一定数量的玉米可以购买的劳力数量的变化而有赔偿责任。 但是,为任何其他商品预留的租金不仅取决于任何特定数量的玉米能够购买的劳动力数量的变化,而且取决于任何特定数量的玉米能够购买的玉米数量的变化。

p15.original: Though the real value of a corn rent, it is to be observed, however, varies much less from century to century than that of a money rent, it varies much more from year to year. The money price of labour, as I shall endeavour to shew hereafter, does not fluctuate from year to year with the money price of corn, but seems to be everywhere accommodated, not to the temporary or occasional, but to the average or ordinary price of that necessary of life. The average or ordinary price of corn, again is regulated, as I shall likewise endeavour to shew hereafter, by the value of silver, by the richness or barrenness of the mines which supply the market with that metal, or by the quantity of labour which must be employed, and consequently of corn which must be consumed, in order to bring any particular quantity of silver from the mine to the market. But the value of silver, though it sometimes varies greatly from century to century, seldom varies much from year to year, but frequently continues the same, or very nearly the same, for half a century or a century together. The ordinary or average money price of corn, therefore, may, during so long a period, continue the same, or very nearly the same, too, and along with it the money price of labour, provided, at least, the society continues, in other respects, in the same, or nearly in the same, condition. In the mean time, the temporary and occasional price of corn may frequently be double one year of what it had been the year before, or fluctuate, for example, from five-and-twenty to fifty shillings the quarter. But when corn is at the latter price, not only the nominal, but the real value of a corn rent, will be double of what it is when at the former, or will command double the quantity either of labour, or of the greater part of other commodities; the money price of labour, and along with it that of most other things, continuing the same during all these fluctuations.
p15.zh: 尽管玉米租金的实际价值,但值得注意的是,与货币租金相比,各世纪的差别要小得多,但每年的差别要大得多。今后我将努力努力提高劳动力的物价,但不会随着玉米的物价而年年波动,而是似乎随处可见,不是临时或偶然的,而是这种生活需要的平均或普通价格。 同样,玉米的平均或普通价格也受到管制,因为我今后同样要努力以银的价值、以金属供应市场的矿山的丰富或贫瘠程度、或必须雇用的劳动力数量、以及因此必须消费的玉米数量来施展,以便将矿山的任何特定数量的银元带入市场。 但银币的价值虽然有时在世纪间差异很大,但年复一年的差别很少,但经常会维持同样或几乎相同的银币价值,持续半个世纪或一个世纪。 因此,玉米的普通价格或平均价格在如此长的一段时间内,可能继续维持同样或几乎一样,并随之维持劳动力的货币价格,但至少社会在其他方面继续维持同样或几乎一样的状况。 在平均时间内,玉米的临时和不定期价格可能经常是前一年的两倍,或者波动,例如从季度的5先令和20先令到50先令。 但是,当玉米价格达到后一种价格时, 不仅名义价格,而且玉米租金的实际价值, 将会是前者价格的两倍, 或者会得到两倍于劳动力的数量, 或者更多其他商品的数量; 劳动力的货币价格, 以及与之相关的大多数其他东西的价格, 在所有这些波动中, 都会保持同样的水平。

p16.original: Labour, therefore, it appears evidently, is the only universal, as well as the only accurate, measure of value, or the only standard by which we can compare the values of different commodities, at all times, and at all places. We cannot estimate, it is allowed, the real value of different commodities from century to century by the quantities of silver which were given for them. We cannot estimate it from year to year by the quantities of corn. By the quantities of labour, we can, with the greatest accuracy, estimate it, both from century to century, and from year to year. From century to century, corn is a better measure than silver, because, from century to century, equal quantities of corn will command the same quantity of labour more nearly than equal quantities of silver. From year to year, on the contrary, silver is a better measure than corn, because equal quantities of it will more nearly command the same quantity of labour.
p16.zh: 因此,显然,劳动力是唯一的普世价值,也是唯一的准确价值衡量标准,也是我们能够在所有时间和所有地点比较不同商品价值的唯一标准。 我们无法估计 -- -- 允许 -- -- 不同商品的实际价值 -- -- 以所赠送的银子数量计算。 我们不能逐年估计玉米的数量。 从劳动力数量来看,我们可以最准确地估计,无论是从世纪到世纪,还是从一年到一年。 从一个世纪到一个世纪,玉米比银的计量要好,因为从一个世纪到一个世纪,同样数量的玉米会得到同样数量的劳动力,比同等数量的银要多. 相反,银子年复一年地比玉米更能衡量,因为同等数量银子将更接近于获得同样数量的劳动力。

p17.original: But though, in establishing perpetual rents, or even in letting very long leases, it may be of use to distinguish between real and nominal price; it is of none in buying and selling, the more common and ordinary transactions of human life.
p17.zh: 但是,在确定永久租金,甚至租借很长的租金时,区分实际价格和名义价格可能是有益的;在买卖方面,这是人类生活中更为常见和普通的交易。

p18.original: At the same time and place, the real and the nominal price of all commodities are exactly in proportion to one another. The more or less money you get for any commodity, in the London market, for example, the more or less labour it will at that time and place enable you to purchase or command. At the same time and place, therefore, money is the exact measure of the real exchangeable value of all commodities. It is so, however, at the same time and place only.
p18.zh: 同时和地点,所有商品的实际价格和名义价格都完全按照彼此的比例来分配.伦敦市场里的任何商品,你都能得到多少钱, 比如说,在那个时候和地点,它能多少或多或少地获得劳力, 让你能够购买或指挥。 因此,在时间和地点上,货币是衡量所有商品实际可兑换价值的确切尺度。 然而,它只是在同一时间和地点。

p19.original: Though at distant places there is no regular proportion between the real and the money price of commodities, yet the merchant who carries goods from the one to the other, has nothing to consider but the money price, or the difference between the quantity of silver for which he buys them, and that for which he is likely to sell them. Half an ounce of silver at Canton in China may command a greater quantity both of labour and of the necessaries and conveniencies of life, than an ounce at London. A commodity, therefore, which sells for half an ounce of silver at Canton, may there be really dearer, of more real importance to the man who possesses it there, than a commodity which sells for an ounce at London is to the man who possesses it at London. If a London merchant, however, can buy at Canton, for half an ounce of silver, a commodity which he can afterwards sell at London for an ounce, he gains a hundred per cent. by the bargain, just as much as if an ounce of silver was at London exactly of the same value as at Canton. It is of no importance to him that half an ounce of silver at Canton would have given him the command of more labour, and of a greater quantity of the necessaries and conveniencies of life than an ounce can do at London. An ounce at London will always give him the command of double the quantity of all these, which half an ounce could have done there, and this is precisely what he wants.
p19.zh: 虽然在遥远的地方,商品的实际价格和货币价格之间没有固定的比例,然而从一个到另一个的运货商,除了货币价格,或者他购买的银的数量与他可能出售的银的数量之间的差额,没有什么可考虑的.在中国的坎顿,半盎司的白银可能比在伦敦的一盎司得到更多的劳动力和生活必需品和方便。 因此,一种商品,在坎顿卖了半盎司的银子, 可能真的更珍贵, 对那里拥有它的人来说更重要, 比在伦敦卖一盎司的商品, 对在伦敦拥有它的人来说更重要。 但是,如果伦敦商人能在坎顿购买半盎司的银子,而这一商品之后他可以在伦敦出售一盎司,那么他通过交易获得100%的收益,就像一盎司的银子在伦敦的价值与在坎顿一样。 在坎顿半盎司的白银 本来会给他更多的劳动力 以及更多的生活必需品 和方便 对他来说,这不重要 伦敦一盎司可以做的。在伦敦一盎司会总是给他 两倍于所有这些数量的命令, 半盎司可以在那里做, 而这正是他想要的。

p20.original: As it is the nominal or money price of goods, therefore, which finally determines the prudence or imprudence of all purchases and sales, and thereby regulates almost the whole business of common life in which price is concerned, we cannot wonder that it should have been so much more attended to than the real price.
p20.zh: 因此,货物的名义价格或货币价格最终决定了所有采购和销售的谨慎或不当性,从而几乎规范了涉及价格的共同生活中的整个业务,因此,我们不禁要问,它是否应该比实际价格得到如此多的注意。

p21.original: In such a work as this, however, it may sometimes be of use to compare the different real values of a particular commodity at different times and places, or the different degrees of power over the labour of other people which it may, upon different occasions, have given to those who possessed it. We must in this case compare, not so much the different quantities of silver for which it was commonly sold, as the different quantities or labour which those different quantities of silver could have purchased. But the current prices of labour, at distant times and places, can scarce ever be known with any degree of exactness. Those of corn, though they have in few places been regularly recorded, are in general better known, and have been more frequently taken notice of by historians and other writers. We must generally, therefore, content ourselves with them, not as being always exactly in the same proportion as the current prices of labour, but as being the nearest approximation which can commonly be had to that proportion. I shall hereafter have occasion to make several comparisons of this kind.
p21.zh: 然而,在这类工作中,有时比较某一商品在不同时间和地点的不同实际价值,或比较它在不同场合可能赋予拥有这种商品的人的对其他人的劳动的不同程度的权力,可能是有益的。 在此情况下,我们必须比较不同数量的白银,而不是一般出售的白银,作为这些不同数量的白银可以购买的不同数量或劳动力。 但是,在遥远的时间和地点,目前劳动力的价格几乎无法确切地知道。玉米的玉米虽然在少数地方有定期记录,但总的来说比较有名,历史学家和其他作家也更经常注意到这些玉米。 因此,我们一般必须满足于它们,不是始终与目前的劳动力价格完全相同,而是作为最接近的近似值,通常可以达到这个比例。 我今后将有机会进行若干次这种比较。

p22.original: In the progress of industry, commercial nations have found it convenient to coin several different metals into money; gold for larger payments, silver for purchases of moderate value, and copper, or some other coarse metal, for those of still smaller consideration, They have always, however, considered one of those metals as more peculiarly the measure of value than any of the other two; and this preference seems generally to have been given to the metal which they happen first to make use of as the instrument of commerce. Having once begun to use it as their standard, which they must have done when they had no other money, they have generally continued to do so even when the necessity was not the same.
p22.zh: 在工业进步中,商业国家发现将几种不同的金属硬化为货币是方便的;黄金用于更大的付款,白银用于购买中值,铜或一些其他粗金属,对于那些考虑仍然较小的金属,它们总是认为其中一种金属比其他两种金属更特别地成为价值的衡量标准;这种偏好似乎一般是放在它们首先用作商业工具的金属上。 他们一度开始将其作为标准,而当他们没有其他钱时,他们一定是这样做的,因此,他们一般都继续这样做,即使必要性不同。

p23.original: The Romans are said to have had nothing but copper money till within five years before the first Punic war (Pliny, lib. xxxiii. cap. 3), when they first began to coin silver. Copper, therefore, appears to have continued always the measure of value in that republic. At Rome all accounts appear to have been kept, and the value of all estates to have been computed, either in asses or in sestertii. The as was always the denomination of a copper coin. The word sestertius signifies two asses and a half. Though the sestertius, therefore, was originally a silver coin, its value was estimated in copper. At Rome, one who owed a great deal of money was said to have a great deal of other people's copper.
p23.zh: 据说罗马人除了铜钱,在第一次普尼奇战争前的五年内(普利尼, lib. xxii. cap)什么都没有.3),当他们第一次开始铸造银币时. 因此,铜似乎始终是该共和国价值的衡量标准。在罗马,所有的账户似乎都保留了下来,所有财产的价值都计算在驴子或塞斯特提(sestatii)中。铜币的面额一直如此。塞斯特提乌斯这个词意味着两个半驴子 因此,虽然塞斯特提乌斯原本是一枚银币,但其价值以铜币估算.在罗马,一个欠下大笔钱的人据说拥有大量其他人的铜器.

p24.original: The northern nations who established themselves upon the ruins of the Roman empire, seem to have had silver money from the first beginning of their settlements, and not to have known either gold or copper coins for several ages thereafter. There were silver coins in England in the time of the Saxons; but there was little gold coined till the time of Edward III nor any copper till that of James I. of Great Britain. In England, therefore, and for the same reason, I believe, in all other modern nations of Europe, all accounts are kept, and the value of all goods and of all estates is generally computed, in silver: and when we mean to express the amount of a person's fortune, we seldom mention the number of guineas, but the number of pounds sterling which we suppose would be given for it.
p24.zh: 罗马帝国废墟上建立自己的北方诸国,似乎从最初的定居点开始就有银钱,此后数年里都不了解金币或铜币. 在萨克森人时代英格兰有银币;但直到爱德华三世时期,几乎没有金币铸造,也没有铜币铸造到大不列颠的詹姆斯一世. 因此,在英国,出于同样的原因,我相信,在欧洲其他所有现代国家,所有帐户都保留下来,所有商品和所有庄园的价值一般都用银子计算:当我们想表达一个人财富的金额时,我们很少提到豚鼠的数量,但是我们推测会为此付出的英镑的数量.

p25.original: Originally, in all countries, I believe, a legal tender of payment could be made only in the coin of that metal which was peculiarly considered as the standard or measure of value. In England, gold was not considered as a legal tender for a long time after it was coined into money. The proportion between the values of gold and silver money was not fixed by any public law or proclamation, but was left to be settled by the market. If a debtor offered payment in gold, the creditor might either reject such payment altogether, or accept of it at such a valuation of the gold as he and his debtor could agree upon. Copper is not at present a legal tender, except in the change of the smaller silver coins.
p25.zh: 我认为,最初,在所有国家,只能用这种被特别视为价值标准或计量的金属硬币来合法支付。 在英国,黄金在铸造成钱币后很长时间内不被视为合法投标. 金银币价值的比例没有受到任何公法或公告的确定,而是留给市场解决. 如果债务人提出用黄金付款,债权人可以完全拒绝这种付款,或者在与债务人商定的黄金估值时接受这种付款。铜目前不是法定货币,只有较小的银币的变更除外.

p26.original: In this state of things, the distinction between the metal which was the standard, and that which was not the standard, was something more than a nominal distinction.
p26.zh: 在这种状态下,作为标准的金属与不是标准的金属之间的区别,不仅仅是名义上的区别。

p27.original: In process of time, and as people became gradually more familiar with the use of the different metals in coin, and consequently better acquainted with the proportion between their respective values, it has, in most countries, I believe, been found convenient to ascertain this proportion, and to declare by a public law, that a guinea, for example, of such a weight and fineness, should exchange for one-and-twenty shillings, or be a legal tender for a debt of that amount. In this state of things, and during the continuance of any one regulated proportion of this kind, the distinction between the metal, which is the standard, and that which is not the standard, becomes little more than a nominal distinction.
p27.zh: 随着时间的推移,随着人们逐渐更加熟悉硬币中不同金属的使用,从而更熟悉各自价值的比例,我认为,在大多数国家,确定这一比例和通过公法宣布,例如如此重量和罚款的几内亚币应换1至20先令,或成为这一数额的债务的合法报价。 在目前的状况下,在任何一种规范的这种比例的延续中,金属(即标准)与非标准之间的区别,几乎只是名义上的区别。

p28.original: In consequence of any change, however, in this regulated proportion, this distinction becomes, or at least seems to become, something more than nominal again. If the regulated value of a guinea, for example, was either reduced to twenty, or raised to two-and-twenty shillings, all accounts being kept, and almost all obligations for debt being expressed, in silver money, the greater part of payments could in either case be made with the same quantity of silver money as before; but would require very different quantities of gold money; a greater in the one case, and a smaller in the other. Silver would appear to be more invariable in its value than gold. Silver would appear to measure the value of gold, and gold would not appear to measure the value of silver. The value of gold would seem to depend upon the quantity of silver which it would exchange for, and the value of silver would not seem to depend upon the quantity of gold which it would exchange for. This difference, however, would be altogether owing to the custom of keeping accounts, and of expressing the amount of all great and small sums rather in silver than in gold money. One of Mr Drummond's notes for five-and-twenty or fifty guineas would, after an alteration of this kind, be still payable with five-and-twenty or fifty guineas, in the same manner as before. It would, after such an alteration, be payable with the same quantity of gold as before, but with very different quantities of silver. In the payment of such a note, gold would appear to be more invariable in its value than silver. Gold would appear to measure the value of silver, and silver would not appear to measure the value of gold. If the custom of keeping accounts, and of expressing promissory-notes and other obligations for money, in this manner should ever become general, gold, and not silver, would be considered as the metal which was peculiarly the standard or measure of value.
p28.zh: 然而,由于任何变化,在这种受管制的比例方面,这种区别会变成,或者至少看起来会变成比名义上的更严重的区别。 例如,如果几内亚尼的管制价值减少至20先令,或增加到2先令和20先令,所有账户都保留,几乎所有债务债务都以银币表示,那么在这两种情况下,大部分付款都可以用与以前相同的银币数额支付;但需要非常不同的金币数额;在一种情况下,数额更大,而在另一种情况下,数额较小。白银的价值似乎比黄金更不可改变。白银似乎可以测量黄金的价值,而白金似乎不能测量白银的价值.黄金的价值似乎取决于它所交换的银的数量,而银的价值似乎并不取决于它所交换的金的数量。 然而,这种差异完全是由于保持账户的习惯,以及用银而不是金币表示所有大数额和小数额。德鲁蒙德先生的一张五和二十或五十几尼的纸币 在这种修改之后 仍然可以以和以前一样的方式支付五和二十或五十几尼的票价 在进行这种改装后,应支付与以前相同的黄金,但银的数量却大不相同。 在支付这种纸币时,黄金的价值似乎比白银更不可改变。黄金似乎可以衡量银的价值,而银似乎不能衡量金的价值。 如果记账和表示本票和其他货币债务的习惯,以这种方式成为一般做法,黄金而不是银子,将被视为一种特殊地是价值标准或计量的金属。

p29.original: In reality, during the continuance of any one regulated proportion between the respective values of the different metals in coin, the value of the most precious metal regulates the value of the whole coin. Twelve copper pence contain half a pound avoirdupois of copper, of not the best quality, which, before it is coined, is seldom worth seven-pence in silver. But as, by the regulation, twelve such pence are ordered to exchange for a shilling, they are in the market considered as worth a shilling, and a shilling can at any time be had for them. Even before the late reformation of the gold coin of Great Britain, the gold, that part of it at least which circulated in London and its neighbourhood, was in general less degraded below its standard weight than the greater part of the silver. One-and-twenty worn and defaced shillings, however, were considered as equivalent to a guinea, which, perhaps, indeed, was worn and defaced too, but seldom so much so. The late regulations have brought the gold coin as near, perhaps, to its standard weight as it is possible to bring the current coin of any nation; and the order to receive no gold at the public offices but by weight, is likely to preserve it so, as long as that order is enforced. The silver coin still continues in the same worn and degraded state as before the reformation of the cold coin. In the market, however, one-and-twenty shillings of this degraded silver coin are still considered as worth a guinea of this excellent gold coin.
p29.zh: 实际上,在任何一种硬币上对不同金属的各自价值的比例进行管制的继续期间,最贵金属的价值对整枚硬币的价值进行管制。十二便士中含有半磅的铜,质量不高,在铸币前,很少值七便士的银币. 但是,根据条例,12个这样的便士被命令换取一先令,他们被市场视为价值一先令,随时都可以为他们获得一先令。即使在大不列颠的金币晚期改革之前,黄金,至少是在伦敦及其邻近地区流通的那部分金币,其退化程度一般低于其标准重量,低于银币的较大部分. 然而,有20先令的磨损和变质被视为相当于一种豚鼠,而这种豚鼠也许也曾磨损和变质,但很少如此。后期的条例使金币接近,也许达到标准重量,只要有可能使任何国家的现成硬币得到;而且只要执行这项命令,在公职部门不接收金币的命令就有可能保留下来,但按重量计算。银币仍然和冷币改制前一样,在磨损和退化的状态下继续存在. 然而,在市场上,这种退化的银币的1先令和20先令仍然被认为是这一优秀的金币的一毛钱.

p30.original: The reformation of the gold coin has evidently raised the value of the silver coin which can be exchanged for it.
p30.zh: 改革金币显然提高了可以兑换的银币的价值。

p31.original: In the English mint, a pound weight of gold is coined into forty-four guineas and a half, which at one-and-twenty shillings the guinea, is equal to forty-six pounds fourteen shillings and sixpence. An ounce of such gold coin, therefore, is worth £ 3:17:10½ in silver. In England, no duty or seignorage is paid upon the coinage, and he who carries a pound weight or an ounce weight of standard gold bullion to the mint, gets back a pound weight or an ounce weight of gold in coin, without any deduction. Three pounds seventeen shillings and tenpence halfpenny an ounce, therefore, is said to be the mint price of gold in England, or the quantity of gold coin which the mint gives in return for standard gold bullion.
p31.zh: 在英国薄荷酒中,一磅重的金币被铸造成四十四金币和半金币,在一二十先令时,金币等于四十六英磅十四先令和六便士. 因此,这种金币的一盎司价值为3:17:101⁄2英镑的银币. 在英国,硬币上不支付任何关税或铸币,而携带一磅重或一盎司标准金金金币到薄荷币的人,在硬币上获得一磅重或一盎司金币重量,而无需扣除任何费用. 因此,据说3英磅17先令和1盎司的10便士是英国金币的薄荷价格,或者薄荷作为标准金币的回报而提供的金币数量.

p32.original: Before the reformation of the gold coin, the price of standard gold bullion in the market had, for many years, been upwards of £3:18s. sometimes £ 3:19s, and very frequently £4 an ounce; that sum, it is probable, in the worn and degraded gold coin, seldom containing more than an ounce of standard gold. Since the reformation of the gold coin, the market price of standard gold bullion seldom exceeds £ 3:17:7 an ounce. Before the reformation of the gold coin, the market price was always more or less above the mint price. Since that reformation, the market price has been constantly below the mint price. But that market price is the same whether it is paid in gold or in silver coin. The late reformation of the gold coin, therefore, has raised not only the value of the gold coin, but likewise that of the silver coin in proportion to gold bullion, and probably, too, in proportion to all other commodities; though the price of the greater part of other commodities being influenced by so many other causes, the rise in the value of either gold or silver coin in proportion to them may not be so distinct and sensible.
p32.zh: 在金币改革前,市场标准金币的价格多年来一直上扬3:18英镑. 有时是3:19英镑,而且非常经常是4英镑一盎司;在已磨损和退化的金币中,这一数额很可能是很少包含超过一盎司标准金币的. 自金币改制以来,标准金币的市场价格很少超过每盎司3:17:7英镑. 在金币改制前,市场价格总是或多或少高于薄荷价格. 自改革以来,市场价格一直低于薄荷价格。 但无论以金币还是银币支付,市场价格都是一样的. 因此,金币的晚期改制不仅提高了金币的价值,同样提高了银币与金金牛金币的比例,很可能也提高了其他商品的比例;虽然其他商品中大部分的价格受到如此众多其他原因的影响,但金币或银币按其比例的上涨可能并不那么明显和合理.

p33.original: In the English mint, a pound weight of standard silver bullion is coined into sixty-two shillings, containing, in the same manner, a pound weight of standard silver. Five shillings and twopence an ounce, therefore, is said to be the mint price of silver in England, or the quantity of silver coin which the mint gives in return for standard silver bullion. Before the reformation of the gold coin, the market price of standard silver bullion was, upon different occasions, five shillings and fourpence, five shillings and fivepence, five shillings and sixpence, five shillings and sevenpence, and very often five shillings and eightpence an ounce. Five shillings and sevenpence, however, seems to have been the most common price. Since the reformation of the gold coin, the market price of standard silver bullion has fallen occasionally to five shillings and threepence, five shillings and fourpence, and five shillings and fivepence an ounce, which last price it has scarce ever exceeded. Though the market price of silver bullion has fallen considerably since the reformation of the gold coin, it has not fallen so low as the mint price.
p33.zh: 在英国薄荷酒中,标准银金币的一磅重被硬币铸成62先令,同样含有标准银币的一磅重. 因此,据说5先令和2便士一盎司是英国银的薄荷价格,或者薄荷作为标准银金币的回报而提供的银币数量. 在金币改制前,标准银金币的市场价格在不同场合是五先令和四便士,五先令和五便士,五先令和六便士,五先令和七便士,经常是五先令和八便士一盎司. 然而,5先令和7便士似乎是最常见的价格。 自金币改制以来,标准银金币的市场价格偶尔会下跌至5先令和3便士,5先令和4便士,5先令和5便士一盎司,这是它从未超过的最后价格. 虽然自金币改制以来,银金币的市场价格大幅下跌,但并没有像薄荷价格那样低落.

p34.original: In the proportion between the different metals in the English coin, as copper is rated very much above its real value, so silver is rated somewhat below it. In the market of Europe, in the French coin and in the Dutch coin, an ounce of fine gold exchanges for about fourteen ounces of fine silver. In the English coin, it exchanges for about fifteen ounces, that is, for more silver than it is worth, according to the common estimation of Europe. But as the price of copper in bars is not, even in England, raised by the high price of copper in English coin, so the price of silver in bullion is not sunk by the low rate of silver in English coin. Silver in bullion still preserves its proper proportion to gold, for the same reason that copper in bars preserves its proper proportion to silver.
p34.zh: 在英国硬币中不同金属之间的比例上,由于铜被评为远高于其实际价值,所以银分略低于其额.在欧洲市场,在法国硬币和荷兰硬币中,一盎司的精制金币交换约14盎司的精制银币. 在英国的硬币中,它交换了大约15盎司,即根据欧洲的共同估计,银币比价值还要多. 但是,由于酒吧中的铜价甚至英国也没有因为英国硬币中的铜价高涨而上涨,所以金牛座中的银价并没有因为英国硬币中的银价低而下沉. 金银制银仍然保持其与金的恰当比例,同样的原因,酒吧中的铜保持其与银的恰当比例.

p35.original: Upon the reformation of the silver coin, in the reign of William III., the price of silver bullion still continued to be somewhat above the mint price. Mr Locke imputed this high price to the permission of exporting silver bullion, and to the prohibition of exporting silver coin. This permission of exporting, he said, rendered the demand for silver bullion greater than the demand for silver coin. But the number of people who want silver coin for the common uses of buying and selling at home, is surely much greater than that of those who want silver bullion either for the use of exportation or for any other use. There subsists at present a like permission of exporting gold bullion, and a like prohibition of exporting gold coin; and yet the price of gold bullion has fallen below the mint price. But in the English coin, silver was then, in the same manner as now, under-rated in proportion to gold; and the gold coin (which at that time, too, was not supposed to require any reformation) regulated then, as well as now, the real value of the whole coin. As the reformation of the silver coin did not then reduce the price of silver bullion to the mint price, it is not very probable that a like reformation will do so now.
p35.zh: 银币改革后,在威廉三世统治时期,银金币的价格仍然略高于薄荷币的价格.洛克先生将这一高价归咎于允许出口银块,以及禁止出口银币。 他说,这种出口许可使得对银块的需求大于对银币的需求. 但是,为了在国内购买和销售的普通用途而想要银币的人,肯定比为了出口或任何其他用途而想要银金币的人要多得多。 目前,金块出口的许可和金币出口的禁令都存在,但金块的价格却低于薄荷价格。 但在英国硬币中,银币当时以与现在相同的方式,按照金币的比例被低估;而金币(当时也不应该要求任何改革)则在当时以及现在对整枚硬币的实际价值进行调节. 由于银币的重新铸造并没有将银金币的价格降低到薄荷价格,因此现在类似重新铸造的银金币不太可能会这样做.

p36.original: Were the silver coin brought back as near to its standard weight as the gold, a guinea, it is probable, would, according to the present proportion, exchange for more silver in coin than it would purchase in bullion. The silver coin containing its full standard weight, there would in this case, be a profit in melting it down, in order, first to sell the bullion for gold coin, and afterwards to exchange this gold coin for silver coin, to be melted down in the same manner. Some alteration in the present proportion seems to be the only method of preventing this inconveniency.
p36.zh: 如果将银币带回接近其标准重量的金币,根据目前的比例,很可能用金币换取比用金块购买更多的银币。包含其全部标准重量的银币,在这种情况下,熔化后会有利润,以便首先将金币的金币出售,然后将这枚金币换成银币,以同样的方式熔化.改变目前的比例似乎是防止这种不方便的唯一办法。

p37.original: The inconveniency, perhaps, would be less, if silver was rated in the coin as much above its proper proportion to gold as it is at present rated below it, provided it was at the same time enacted, that silver should not be a legal tender for more than the change of a guinea, in the same manner as copper is not a legal tender for more than the change of a shilling. No creditor could, in this case, be cheated in consequence of the high valuation of silver in coin; as no creditor can at present be cheated in consequence of the high valuation of copper. The bankers only would suffer by this regulation. When a run comes upon them, they sometimes endeavour to gain time, by paying in sixpences, and they would be precluded by this regulation from this discreditable method of evading immediate payment. They would be obliged, in consequence, to keep at all times in their coffers a greater quantity of cash than at present; and though this might, no doubt, be a considerable inconveniency to them, it would, at the same time, be a considerable security to their creditors.
p37.zh: 如果在硬币上对白银的评分高于其目前对金币的评分,如果同时颁布的话,那么不方便的情况可能就更少了。 白银不应是改变豚鼠币的法定标价,与改变一先令的铜一样,白银不应是改变一先令的法定标价。 在这种情况下,任何债权人都不能因为硬币中的银值很高而被欺骗;因为目前没有任何债权人由于铜值很高而被欺骗。银行家只受这一条例的制约。 当跑来时,他们有时试图通过六便士付款来争取时间,而这一条例将阻止他们采取这种可耻的逃避即时付款的方法。 因此,它们必须随时将比目前更多的现金存入国库;尽管这无疑对他们来说可能是相当不方便的,但与此同时,这对其债权人来说也是相当可观的担保。

p38.original: Three pounds seventeen shillings and tenpence halfpenny (the mint price of gold) certainly does not contain, even in our present excellent gold coin, more than an ounce of standard gold, and it may be thought, therefore, should not purchase more standard bullion. But gold in coin is more convenient than gold in bullion; and though, in England, the coinage is free, yet the gold which is carried in bullion to the mint, can seldom be returned in coin to the owner till after a delay of several weeks. In the present hurry of the mint, it could not be returned till after a delay of several months. This delay is equivalent to a small duty, and renders gold in coin somewhat more valuable than an equal quantity of gold in bullion. If, in the English coin, silver was rated according to its proper proportion to gold, the price of silver bullion would probably fall below the mint price, even without any reformation of the silver coin; the value even of the present worn and defaced silver coin being regulated by the value of the excellent gold coin for which it can be changed.
p38.zh: 3磅17先令和10便士半便士(金币的薄荷价格)当然不包含,即使在我们目前出色的金币中,也不仅仅包含一盎司的标准金币,因此可以认为不应该购买更多的标准金币. 但硬币中的金币比金币中的金币更方便;虽然在英国,硬币是免费的,然而,金币中携带到薄荷的金币,很少能以硬币形式还给所有者,直到拖延数周之后. 在目前急于生产薄荷时,在拖延了几个月之后才能归还。 这种拖延相当于一个小关税,使硬币中的金币比金币中同等数量的金币更有价值。 如果在英国硬币中,银币按其与金币的恰当比例进行评级,那么银金币的价格很可能会跌至薄荷价格以下,即使银币没有进行任何改革;即使是现在磨损的和破损的银币,其价值也会受到能够改变的优秀金币价值的调节.

p39.original: A small seignorage or duty upon the coinage of both gold and silver, would probably increase still more the superiority of those metals in coin above an equal quantity of either of them in bullion. The coinage would, in this case, increase the value of the metal coined in proportion to the extent of this small duty, for the same reason that the fashion increases the value of plate in proportion to the price of that fashion. The superiority of coin above bullion would prevent the melting down of the coin, and would discourage its exportation. If, upon any public exigency, it should become necessary to export the coin, the greater part of it would soon return again, of its own accord. Abroad, it could sell only for its weight in bullion. At home, it would buy more than that weight. There would be a profit, therefore, in bringing it home again. In France, a seignorage of about eight per cent. is imposed upon the coinage, and the French coin, when exported, is said to return home again, of its own accord.
p39.zh: 在金银两币面上作小的铸币或关税,可能使金银币上这些金属的优越性进一步超过金银币中两者中任何一种的同等数量。 在这种情况下,硬币会按照这种小关税的大小比例增加铸币的金属价值,同样的原因是时尚会按照这种时尚的价格比例增加板块价值.硬币在金砖之上的优越性将防止硬币的熔化,并阻止其出口。 如果在任何公众紧急需要时,必须出口该硬币,那么,大部分硬币将很快会自动返回。在国外,它只能卖 其重量在金块。在家里,它会买 更多的重量。 因此,如果把它带回家,将会产生好处。 在法国,硬币上硬币的铸币比例为8%左右,而法国硬币出口时据说会自发地再次回国.

p40.original: The occasional fluctuations in the market price of gold and silver bullion arise from the same causes as the like fluctuations in that of all other commodities. The frequent loss of those metals from various accidents by sea and by land, the continual waste of them in gilding and plating, in lace and embroidery, in the wear and tear of coin, and in that of plate, require, in all countries which possess no mines of their own, a continual importation, in order to repair this loss and this waste. The merchant importers, like all other merchants, we may believe, endeavour, as well as they can, to suit their occasional importations to what they judge is likely to be the immediate demand. With all their attention, however, they sometimes overdo the business, and sometimes underdo it. When they import more bullion than is wanted, rather than incur the risk and trouble of exporting it again, they are sometimes willing to sell a part of it for something less than the ordinary or average price. When, on the other hand, they import less than is wanted, they get something more than this price. But when, under all those occasional fluctuations, the market price either of gold or silver bullion continues for several years together steadily and constantly, either more or less above, or more or less below the mint price, we may be assured that this steady and constant, either superiority or inferiority of price, is the effect of something in the state of the coin, which, at that time, renders a certain quantity of coin either of more value or of less value than the precise quantity of bullion which it ought to contain. The constancy and steadiness of the effect supposes a proportionable constancy and steadiness in the cause.
p40.zh: 金银金币的市场价格偶尔波动,其原因与所有其他商品的类似波动相同。海上和陆上各种事故经常造成这些金属的流失,不断浪费这些金属在镀金和镀金、丝带和刺绣、硬币磨损和板块方面,要求所有没有矿山的国家继续进口这些金属,以弥补这种损失和这种浪费。 我们可能相信,商人进口商同其他所有商家一样,努力并尽其所能,使其偶尔进口的产品符合他们所判断的可能立即需要。 然而,在他们全力以赴的情况下,他们有时会过度经营,有时也会低调经营. 当它们进口的金块比想要的多,而不是再出口金块的风险和麻烦时,它们有时愿意以低于普通价格或平均价格的价格出售一部分金块。 另一方面,当进口量低于预期时,它们得到的比这一价格更高的东西。 但是,在所有这些偶然波动下,金或银金的市场价格持续数年,或多或少高于薄荷价格,或多或少低于薄荷价格,我们可以得到保证,这种稳定不变的价格优劣,是硬币状态下某种东西的影响,在当时,这种作用使一定数量的硬币的价值或多或少于它应该包含的金币的确切数量.效果的坚韧和戒备,假定是因果有一定比例的坚韧和戒备。

p41.original: The money of any particular country is, at any particular time and place, more or less an accurate measure or value, according as the current coin is more or less exactly agreeable to its standard, or contains more or less exactly the precise quantity of pure gold or pure silver which it ought to contain. If in England, for example, forty-four guineas and a half contained exactly a pound weight of standard gold, or eleven ounces of fine gold, and one ounce of alloy, the gold coin of England would be as accurate a measure of the actual value of goods at any particular time and place as the nature of the thing would admit. But if, by rubbing and wearing, forty-four guineas and a half generally contain less than a pound weight of standard gold, the diminution, however, being greater in some pieces than in others, the measure of value comes to be liable to the same sort of uncertainty to which all other weights and measures are commonly exposed. As it rarely happens that these are exactly agreeable to their standard, the merchant adjusts the price of his goods as well as he can, not to what those weights and measures ought to be, but to what, upon an average, he finds, by experience, they actually are. In consequence of a like disorder in the coin, the price of goods comes, in the same manner, to be adjusted, not to the quantity of pure gold or silver which the coin ought to contain, but to that which, upon an average, it is found, by experience, it actually does contain.
p41.zh: 任何特定国家的钱,在任何特定的时间和地点,或多或少是准确的量度或价值,因为目前的硬币或多或少准确符合其标准,或含有或多或少准确的纯金或纯银数量,而其应包含的纯金或纯银. 例如,在英国,四十四个豚鼠和半个鱼鼠中含有精确的磅标准黄金重量,或11盎司精细黄金,以及一盎司合金,那么英格兰的金币就如同该物的性质所承认的那样,是衡量任何特定时间和地点货物实际价值的精确度. 但是,如果通过擦擦和穿戴,44个豚鼠和半豚鼠通常含有低于一磅标准金的重量,但某些金块的缩减比其他金块的缩减更大,那么价值的计量就有可能受到所有其他重量和计量标准通常都暴露在这种不确定性中。 由于很少发生完全符合标准的情况,商人们会尽可能调整其货物的价格,而不是调整其重量和措施,而是调整根据经验,平均而言,他发现它们实际上是什么。 由于硬币上出现类似混乱,商品的价格也以同样的方式出现调整,而不是调整硬币应包含的纯金或银的数量,而是调整到根据经验平均来说确实包含的纯金或银的数量.

p42.original: By the money price of goods, it is to be observed, I understand always the quantity of pure gold or silver for which they are sold, without any regard to the denomination of the coin. Six shillings and eight pence, for example, in the time of Edward I., I consider as the same money price with a pound sterling in the present times, because it contained, as nearly as we can judge, the same quantity of pure silver.
p42.zh: 从商品的货币价格来看,我总是理解它们出售的纯金或银的数量,而不管硬币的面值。 例如,在爱德华一世时代,我把6先令和8便士与现今的英镑视为同样的货币价格,因为它几乎包含着我们所能判断的同样数量的纯银。
